metadata.title: Near AI for VS Code extension

components.title: Extension
components.description: The locally installed VS Code extension.

implemented-requirements.description: The gate decides each request before the settings layer can allow it.

statements.description: The extension sends each tool request through its gate decision function. The floor remains enforced and no setting can turn it off.
statements.remarks: Your organization assigns the approvals and grants the gate evaluates.

implemented-requirements.description: The extension writes gate decision records from its project, workspace-free and sub-agent runtimes to bounded local JSONL logs. The log redacts token-shaped strings.

statements.description: The extension writes gate decision records from its project, workspace-free and sub-agent runtimes to bounded local JSONL logs. The log redacts token-shaped strings.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects the events and components to log, reviews log coverage, and defines retention and forwarding for the deployment.

props.name: limitation
props.value: Local gate decision records cover only extension decisions. They do not establish deployment-wide event selection, retention, or monitoring.

implemented-requirements.description: The extension records gate decision times from its runtime clock as integer milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

statements.description: The extension records gate decision times from its runtime clock as integer milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the required granularity and verifies clock synchronization and timestamp handling for the deployed components.

props.name: limitation
props.value: This evidence covers extension gate decision timestamps. Deployment clock synchronization and timestamp coverage for other components require separate evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: When the extension cannot write its gate decision log, it shows a local VS Code warning. The warning reports the failure once per log writer and omits the storage path.

statements.description: When the extension cannot write its gate decision log, it shows a local VS Code warning. The warning reports the failure once per log writer and omits the storage path.
statements.remarks: Your organization defines the recipients, timing and response actions for audit failures and verifies delivery in the assessed deployment.

props.name: limitation
props.value: The local warning covers extension gate log writes. Delivery to designated operators, capacity warnings and deployment response require separate evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: On POSIX filesystems the extension creates its decision log directory and new log files without group or other access, and retains those permissions through local rotation.

statements.description: On POSIX filesystems the extension creates its decision log directory and new log files without group or other access, and retains those permissions through local rotation.
statements.remarks: Your organization verifies deployment access, audit retention and monitoring, and tests alerts for unauthorized activity.

props.name: limitation
props.value: The result covers freshly created local extension logs on POSIX. Windows ACLs, pre-existing files, same-user tampering, protected storage and unauthorized activity alerts require separate evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Outbound route decision.

statements.description: The route decision refuses content above an endpoint's ceiling and requires the endpoint facts that its policy names.
statements.remarks: Your organization supplies approved endpoint and authorization facts.

implemented-requirements.description: Enforced gate floor.

statements.description: The gate applies its floor before settings and no option can turn that floor off.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which approvals and policy grants to issue.

implemented-requirements.description: Labels on chats.

statements.description: A raised chat label is kept when the chat is reopened and shown beside the selected model.
statements.remarks: Your organization defines labels and handling rules.

implemented-requirements.description: Approval audit event types.

statements.description: The extension emits preflight and preview event types to its configured audit store when it evaluates an approval request.
statements.remarks: Your organization defines the fields required for each approved audit event and verifies coverage and retention in the deployment.

props.name: limitation
props.value: The approval test verifies the extension's preflight and preview audit event types. Required audit fields and coverage across assessed components need separate evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Approval attribution.

statements.description: A forged or stale approval attribution is not accepted as a credential-shaped owner.
statements.remarks: Your organization enrols and administers recognized people and credentials.

props.name: limitation
props.value: Approval attribution is verified for extension decisions. The deployment still needs evidence of authenticator issuance, protection, recovery, rotation and revocation.

implemented-requirements.description: Outbound model check.

statements.description: The outbound route check refuses an unlisted model before it is used.
statements.remarks: Your organization configures endpoints and the network boundary.

implemented-requirements.description: Cryptographic inventory.

statements.description: The extension's crypto inventory records its AES-256-GCM use and the collector reports that entry's documented standing.
statements.remarks: Your organization manages platform secret-storage protection.

props.name: limitation
props.value: The crypto inventory documents the AES-256-GCM entry. It does not establish key management practices or approved cryptographic configurations for a deployment.

implemented-requirements.description: Encrypted project state stored by Git sync.

statements.description: Optional Git project sync stores encrypted objects in the remote repository and refuses modified sealed objects on restore.
statements.remarks: Your organization defines information in scope and verifies protection for local state, hosted stores and backups in the deployment.

props.name: limitation
props.value: This evidence covers encrypted project state stored by the optional Git sync feature. Other local and hosted information stores need separate evidence.

implemented-requirements.description: Sensitive input redaction.

statements.description: Approval previews redact sensitive input before they are presented for approval.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides what its personnel may disclose and retain.

implemented-requirements.description: Third-party encrypted storage remains unsettled.

statements.description: The starting rules keep Controlled Goods content on this computer while third-party encrypted storage remains unresolved.

implemented-requirements.description: TEE eligibility and official decisions remain unsettled.

statements.description: The starting rules keep Controlled Goods content on this computer while TEE eligibility remains unresolved.

implemented-requirements.description: TEE and third-party encrypted storage remain unsettled.

statements.description: The starting rules keep ITAR content on this computer while TEE eligibility remains unresolved.
The starting rules keep ITAR content on this computer while third-party encrypted storage remains unresolved.

control-implementations.description: Statements about the extension from the 44.1 coverage work (44.1-10).

implemented-requirements.description: The signed staff roster is the account record of a multi-user staff project.

statements.description: In a multi-user staff project the signed staff roster is the account record. Only a computer of the staff lead or the deputy lead can invite, admit, change or remove a member; anyone else's attempt is refused and writes nothing. A person is admitted only after the lead confirms the six-word safety code, and the admission records their slot, seat, roles and clearance in a signed roster entry. An invitation expires and works once. Removing a member records the removal and moves every cell key the member held to a new key wrapped only to the devices still cleared. CI tests of the roster prove each of these. Multi-user staff projects are an early preview, off unless a person turns on the setting nearAi.staff.multiUserPreview, and the people and clearances in them are declared by the staff lead, not verified.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who may lead a staff project, approves each person's roles and clearance before they are admitted, reviews the roster on its own schedule and removes people who leave. Accounts in your organization's own directory stay with its identity owners.

implemented-requirements.description: Requests go to an external model service only as your organization's routing rules allow.

statements.description: The extension sends a request to an external model service only as your organization's routing rules allow. A model outside your allowed list is refused. A host your list of places does not name is refused above any-cloud. Content above a place's ceiling is refused, and a place outside the regions your rules name is refused. CI tests of the route gate prove each refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization chooses its external model providers, sets their security requirements in its agreements with them, and keeps the allowed list, the list of places and the regions current.

implemented-requirements.description: The gate records each decision on an agent action, from every runtime, and warns when it cannot.

statements.description: The extension watches each agent action at its gate and writes every decision to a local decision log, from project, workspace-free and sub-agent runtimes alike. When it cannot write the log, it shows a local warning. CI tests of the gate's logs prove both.

props.name: limitation
props.value: Local gate decision records cover only extension decisions. They do not establish deployment-wide event selection, retention, or monitoring.

statements.remarks: Your organization decides what to monitor across the deployment, forwards and reviews the records, and responds to what they show.

implemented-requirements.description: Every account change in a multi-user staff project is a signed roster entry.

statements.description: In a multi-user staff project every account change is written as a signed roster entry: member.admit when a person is admitted, member.remove when a member is removed, member.update when a clearance changes, and deputy.name when a deputy is named, each with the cell key changes it causes. CI tests of the roster prove the entries are written. Multi-user staff projects are an early preview, off unless a person turns on the setting nearAi.staff.multiUserPreview.
statements.remarks: Your organization reviews the roster's entries, tells the people it names when their access changes, and keeps its own records of account actions in its directory.

implemented-requirements.description: The staff lead and the deputy lead are the only roster writers, and naming a deputy is a signed roster entry.

statements.description: A multi-user staff project has two privileged roles, the staff lead and the deputy lead, and only their computers can change the roster. The lead names the deputy with a signed deputy.name entry; the deputy cannot name another deputy, and a planned handover from the deputy is refused. A member's attempt to invite, void, remove or update is refused and changes nothing. CI tests of the roster prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who holds the lead and deputy roles, reviews those assignments, and removes them when a person changes duties.

implemented-requirements.description: The lead can remove a member or cut off one device at once, and the keys they held move on without them.

statements.description: The staff lead or deputy can remove a member, or revoke one of a member's devices, as soon as they decide to. Removal moves every cell key the member held to a new key wrapped only to the devices still cleared, and revoking a device moves only that device's cells. CI tests of the roster prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides when a person poses a risk, tells the staff lead within the time it sets, and records the decision.

implemented-requirements.description: Content leaves for a model service only to a place whose ceiling covers its label, with a pin and an authorization where your rules ask for them.

statements.description: The route gate releases content to a model service only when the place's ceiling in your organization's rules covers the content's label. For Protected B on your organization's own server it also needs the server's pin and a current authorization for that place, project, label and use; an authorization for another place, an expired or revoked one, or one scoped to something else is refused. CI tests of the route gate prove each refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets each place's ceiling, decides which places may receive which labels, and issues and revokes the authorizations.

implemented-requirements.description: Each use of a roster function is a signed entry naming the computer that wrote it.

statements.description: Each use of a staff lead's or deputy's roster function (invite, admit, update, remove, name a deputy) is written as a signed roster entry, and an invitation names the computer that wrote it as the inviter. CI tests of the roster prove the entries and the inviter.
statements.remarks: Your organization reviews the roster's entries and keeps the records of privileged actions in its other systems.

implemented-requirements.description: A member who is not the lead or deputy cannot run a roster function.

statements.description: In a multi-user staff project a member who is not the staff lead or the deputy lead cannot invite, void an invitation, remove a member or change a member: each attempt is refused as not-a-roster-writer and changes nothing. No agent tool can lower a chat's label; only the person's own command does. CI tests prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who holds the lead and deputy roles.

implemented-requirements.description: A chat's label is lowered only by the person, with a reason, and recorded; a copy cannot lower it unsigned.

statements.description: A chat's label only rises on its own. Only the person's Lower This Chat's Label command can lower it, never an agent tool; with an empty reason nothing changes, and with a reason the label is lowered and a label.declassify record holds both labels and the reason. A lowering arriving from another copy is applied only when its signature verifies; a changed byte, another purpose, another chat or an unsigned time is ignored. CI tests of the chat label prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who may lower a label and reviews the label.declassify records.

implemented-requirements.description: The chat's label is shown beside the model and in the status bar.

statements.description: The chat page shows the chat's label as text beside the model, and the status bar shows the label of the chat in view, whenever the label is above the default. CI tests of the chat page and the status text prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the default label and the markings its own documents and outputs carry.

implemented-requirements.description: The extension's pages run only the scripts it ships, under a strict content policy.

statements.description: The extension's pages run only the scripts it ships. Each page loads its scripts with a fresh nonce under a content policy that allows no eval, no inline script and no remote source. CI tests of the pages prove this.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which extensions its people may install in their editor.

implemented-requirements.description: A page cannot load or run code from elsewhere.

statements.description: The content policy of the extension's pages allows no remote source, no eval and no inline script, so a page cannot download code or run code it was not shipped with. CI tests of the pages prove the policy.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which extensions its people may install in their editor.

implemented-requirements.description: An attested request goes only over a connection pinned to the attested key.

statements.description: A request that needs an attested model service goes only over a connection pinned to the key the attestation bound. A connection to another key is rejected before the server sees anything, and when a layer ignores the request's TLS options the live socket is checked so a different server gets nothing. A source that cannot pin is refused, never sent unpinned. CI tests of the connection binding prove each case.

props.name: limitation
props.value: The trust badge's checks do not check TCB status or revocation, enclave measurements, or NVIDIA's verdict

statements.remarks: Your organization decides which model services may receive which labels.

implemented-requirements.description: Optional Git project sync encrypts project state before it leaves the computer and refuses a changed object.

statements.description: Optional Git project sync encrypts project state before it is pushed: after real pushes the remote holds only ciphertext, with no plain text in any blob, tree entry name, commit, message or ref name. On restore, an object with a changed byte is refused as tampered. CI tests of the sync prove both.

props.name: limitation
props.value: This evidence covers encrypted project state stored by the optional Git sync feature. Other local and hosted information stores need separate evidence.

statements.remarks: Your organization decides which information may be synced and protects the remote repository and the computers that hold the key.

implemented-requirements.description: The gate decision log has a fixed size: 5 MiB per file and at most four rotated files.

statements.description: The extension's gate decision log has a fixed size. A file is rotated at 5 MiB, renamed whole before the next line, and at most four rotated files are kept, the oldest dropped first. CI tests of the decision log prove the sizes and the rotation.

props.name: limitation
props.value: Local gate decision records cover only extension decisions. They do not establish deployment-wide event selection, retention, or monitoring.

statements.remarks: Your organization decides how long records must be kept and forwards them to storage it sizes for that before the oldest are dropped.

implemented-requirements.description: Every runtime of the extension writes gate decision records, and each stored record validates.

statements.description: Every runtime of the extension that runs an agent (a project, no folder, a sub-agent, a run with nobody present) writes its gate decision records to disk. Each record is checked against its schema with the sequence number the log gives it before it is stored; a record that is not valid is not written and is reported. CI tests of the decision log prove both.

props.name: limitation
props.value: Local gate decision records cover only extension decisions. They do not establish deployment-wide event selection, retention, or monitoring.

statements.remarks: Your organization selects which events it needs recorded across the deployment and checks that each component records them.

implemented-requirements.description: A request goes only to a place inside the regions your organization's residency rule names.

statements.description: When your organization's rules name regions, the route gate refuses a place outside them (route.residency). A model that NEAR AI forwards to another service has no region, so a Canada residency rule refuses it. This computer and places inside the regions go. CI tests of the route gate prove each case.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides where its information may be processed and stored, names those regions in its rules, and checks its providers' locations in its agreements.

implemented-requirements.description: The extension's tests run in the required CI test job.

statements.description: The extension's unit and integration tests run in the required CI test job on every pull request and main build, and the evidence bundle records that job's result.
statements.remarks: Your organization tests the extension in its own environment before it approves a release for use.
